A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ARROW research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, figures and tables, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original WeatherBench forecasting results, component and rollout ablations, and weather-event case studies in Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds GraphCast comparisons, additional forecast scores, training diagnostics, routing analyses and comparative forecast maps.

M1.justification: The forecasting architecture, RPE, shared/private experts, losses, DQN and alternating fine-tuning procedure are retained. Algorithm 1 makes existing inputs and outputs explicit and changes the counter wording to 'global step'; this does not establish a different learning procedure. Appendix G.2 supplies previously unstated implementation choices.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same WeatherBench/ERA5 data and multivariate global forecasting task. Table 4 and Appendix J report additional pressure-level outputs already included in v1's modeled weather state. The scheduler analyses examine the retained 2018 test population; no new dataset or downstream task is evaluated.

E2.justification: GraphCast, previously cited but not evaluated, becomes an additional comparator across the original variables and horizons in Table 1. All earlier comparators remain; Pangu becoming Pangu-weather is a naming clarification.

E3.justification: Appendix I introduces diagnostic procedures comparing 120h and 354h trajectories through interval frequencies, trajectory lengths and weekly aggregation. The original data splits, resolution, forecast metrics and ablation settings remain unchanged. Appendix G.2's newly disclosed hyperparameters do not establish changed training settings.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations and two weather examples, v2 adds training stability and convergence diagnostics, expert-routing analysis, scheduler behavior across horizons and seasons, and comparative forecast case studies. Appendices D.2 and H–J substantially expand the evidence about optimization, component behavior and forecast errors.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars for forecast performance. The new training curves and routing-frequency distributions are descriptive analyses rather than additions to uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All retained numerical entries in Table 1 are unchanged, and Table 2 changes only equivalent rounding. v2 adds GraphCast scores, Table 4 results for T500, Z850, U500, V500, U1000 and V1000, and findings in Figures 7–16. For example, new Figure 9 reports 6h interval shares of 36.5% at 120h and 12.5% at 354h.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, RPE derivation and metric formulas are retained, with notation and formatting adjustments only. Appendix D.2 adds empirical convergence curves, not a convergence theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about adaptive rollout, multi-interval modeling, spatial encoding and state-of-the-art forecasting with approximately 10% improvements. The added evidence does not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations connecting expert specialization to load balance, interval selection to horizon-dependent error accumulation, and seasonal scheduler behavior to severe-weather episodes. It also interprets comparative forecast artifacts and broadens downstream application arguments. Section 4.2 revises the discussion of graph methods to recognize GraphCast's stronger performance.

D1.justification: v1 provides software and hardware information but few concrete implementation settings. Appendix G.2 adds architecture dimensions, expert counts, optimizer settings, learning rates, warm-up, early stopping, replay-buffer sizes and update schedules. The abstract also adds a code-access URL, substantially improving reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands cited literature on air quality, traffic and navigation, and multimodal time-series forecasting, with new downstream positioning in Appendix K and GraphCast discussion in Appendix E.4. Several earlier contextual references are removed. The central adaptive-rollout novelty claim remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the overall narrative remain intact. Changes include targeted introduction and MoE wording edits, an acknowledgement, conference headers, and restructuring the former A.1–A.7 appendix headings into separate appendices. Much of the expansion consists of new technical and analytical content rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Figures 7–16 introduce training curves, routing distributions, scheduler diagnostics and extensive comparative forecast maps. Table 4 is new, and Table 1 gains GraphCast columns. Existing figures are retained with some relocation, while Figure 2 receives an expanded caption and Table 2 revises highlighting.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves assessability by filling important architecture and training-documentation gaps in Appendix G.2 and providing a code-access pointer. The GraphCast comparison and new convergence and routing analyses strengthen empirical support beyond v1's ablations and two examples. These gains outweigh localized reporting problems, including Section 4.2's incorrect Table 4 references and Figure 13's 234h/222h mismatch; the new storm-association arguments remain correlational.
